title: Seven Top AI Companies Pledge $4.5T to Off-Balance-Sheet Infrastructure Spending

tickers.name: Alphabet Inc. Class A Common Stock
Meta Platforms, Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
The credit risk for technology firms expanding their artificial intelligence capacity is climbing as a new analysis reveals a vast majority of their infrastructure obligations remain hidden from corporate balance sheets. J.P. Morgan estimates that the seven largest AI companies have pledged $4.5 trillion for future data center leases and hardware, with just 15% of those total liabilities recorded as debt. This disparity has caused the cost to insure the companies' debt against default to rise, while hedge funds have reduced their exposure to the sector by 8%, the steepest drop since 2016.

The largest of these off-book obligations belong to Google, at $1.08 trillion, followed by Meta at $810 billion and Microsoft at $575 billion. For some smaller players, the gap is more extreme; Anthropic's off-balance-sheet commitments are more than 100 times its recorded debt. These multiyear agreements secure scarce chips and power capacity, including data center leases that can extend as long as 30 years. Among the five largest operators, roughly 70% of their $1.3 trillion in future lease commitments were added within the last year.

selectedTweets.text:
If you are an AI investor, do not miss this.

The 7 biggest AI companies have committed $4.5 trillion to future data center leases and purchase deals that do not show up as debt on their balance sheets.

Only about 15% of their total obligations are actually on the books, according to J.P. Morgan.

Look at the gap:

Google: $113B on the books, $1.08T off
Anthropic: $8B on, $865B off
Meta: $110B on, $810B off
Microsoft: $110B on, $575B off
Nvidia: $37B on, $422B off
Amazon: $223B on, $419B off
Oracle: $157B on, $322B off

Anthropic's off book commitments are over 100 times bigger than its recorded debt.

The credit market has started to notice. The cost to insure the debt of these AI companies against default is rising fast.

Hedge funds have also cut their exposure by 8%, the biggest pullback since 2016.

And after the midterms, up to 37.5 GW of data centers planned for 2028 could be paused by new state rules.

These companies signed trillions of dollars in future bills, betting AI demand keeps growing.

What happens if it doesn't?

selectedTweets.text:
The hidden AI financial obligations are SKYROCKETING:

Disclosed off-balance-sheet commitments across Alphabet, $GOOGL, Amazon, $AMZN, Meta, $META, Microsoft, $MSFT, Nvidia, $NVDA, Broadcom, $AVGO, Oracle, $ORCL, and SpaceX surged to a record $4.1 trillion in October.

This is up from $3.1 trillion in August and $1.8 trillion in June.

Off-balance-sheet commitments are now more than 4 TIMES the $1.0 trillion in on-balance-sheet debt and leases.

The increase is largely driven by massive future purchase obligations, which climbed to $2.25 trillion from $1.73 trillion, while leases yet to commence rose to $1.39 trillion from $1.12 trillion.

Meanwhile, guarantees and financial backstops jumped to $273 billion from $158 billion, adding another layer of future financial obligations.

Among companies reporting Q3 figures, Meta, $META, added +$195 billion in commitments, Alphabet, $GOOGL, +$164 billion, Amazon, $AMZN, +$131 billion, Microsoft, $MSFT, +$35 billion, and SpaceX +$51 billion.

Notably, Nvidia, Broadcom and Oracle account for another $381 billion of the increase in the updated estimate, although their figures still rely on summer filings rather than Q3 reports.

The $4.1 trillion is just the beginning, with further increases coming as more companies disclose their latest commitments.

selectedTweets.text:
BREAKING: Alphabet, $GOOGL, Meta, $META, Microsoft, $MSFT, Amazon, $AMZN, and Oracle, $ORCL, have now disclosed a record $3.3 trillion in future spending commitments.

These are off-balance-sheet commitments covering data-center spending, future equipment purchases, leases, and other obligations.

$GOOGL accounts for the largest amount at $1.06 trillion, with its disclosed commitments surging nearly +700% over the last year.

$META follows at $866 billion, with nearly half tied to data-center leases that have not yet commenced and payment periods extending up to 30 years.

Meanwhile, Microsoft, $MSFT, has $593 billion in commitments, followed by Amazon, $AMZN, at $453 billion, and Oracle, $ORCL, at $322 billion.

The AI infrastructure buildout is creating an unprecedented pipeline of future financial obligations.
